issues.legal_issue: A revisional court cannot use its supervisory jurisdiction to reappreciate the entire record as a second appeal and upset concurrent findings of conviction without a proper basis for interference.
material_facts: The trial court convicted three accused, and the appellate court upheld their convictions.
In revision, the High Court reexamined the oral and medical evidence in detail and acquitted the accused.

The medical certificate recorded injuries and showed that the complainant had been referred by a police constable on the night of the incident; a defence witness also admitted the contents and his signature on a complaint about the incident.
The Supreme Court found no basis for concluding that the lower courts had overlooked material evidence or reached perverse findings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its revisional jurisdiction; its acquittal was set aside and the convictions upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 397 and 401 CrPC, read with Sections 395 to 401, confer restricted supervisory or revisional powers and do not permit the High Court to exercise a second appellate power. The High Court may examine whether evidence supports the findings and whether they are unreasonable or perverse. Dulichand v. Delhi Administration supports this restricted role. Ram Briksh v. Ambika Yadav involved interference where material evidence had been overlooked and did not justify unrestricted reappreciation.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_challenges_revisional_acquittal and concurrent_lower_court_convictions and high_court_reappraised_entire_record and not material_evidence_overlooked_or_perverse_findings

predicates.criminal_appeal_challenges_revisional_ac: An appeal challenges an acquittal entered by a court exercising revision over a criminal conviction.
predicates.concurrent_lower_court_convictions: The trial court convicted the accused and the appellate court upheld those convictions.
predicates.high_court_reappraised_entire_record: The revisional court reconsidered the evidence in detail and reached its own conclusion on the merits.
predicates.material_evidence_overlooked_or_perverse: The lower courts overlooked material evidence or made findings that were unreasonable or perverse.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a revisional acquittal following concurrent convictions, and the revisional court reappraised the whole record without material evidence having been overlooked or perverse findings having been made below, the acquittal is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: Common intention may be inferred from participants’ coordinated conduct during an assault without proof of a prearranged plan, and minor discrepancies do not by themselves discredit the prosecution case.
material_facts: After a dispute about cleaning a drain, several members of one family entered the complainant’s home and assaulted her, then dragged her outside and beat her repeatedly.
The complainant had four simple injuries recorded in a medical certificate made that night after referral by a police constable.
The complainant’s account was supported by witnesses, while a defence witness admitted signing and the contents of a complaint about the incident.
The High Court relied on discrepancies about the objects used, the alleged number of blows, and the absence of medical examination of a neighbour who intervened.
issues.conclusion: The conduct established common intention to commit house trespass and cause hurt; the discrepancies and omissions identified by the High Court did not justify rejecting the prosecution case.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 IPC does not require proof of a prearranged plot or prior concert in every case; common intention may be established from the participants’ conduct and the circumstances. Exaggeration or minor discrepancies do not necessarily falsify the occurrence or undermine the prosecution case.

rule.if: criminal_case_alleges_joint_offending and multiple_accused_act_together_in_assault and evidence_supports_the_occurrence and discrepancies_are_minor

predicates.criminal_case_alleges_joint_offending: The criminal proceeding alleges that multiple accused jointly committed an offence.
predicates.multiple_accused_act_together_in_assault: More than one accused acted together in carrying out the assault.
predicates.evidence_supports_the_occurrence: Witness or medical evidence supports that the alleged incident occurred.
predicates.discrepancies_are_minor: Differences or omissions in the evidence do not undermine its central account of the incident.

issues.definition: When a criminal case alleges joint offending, multiple accused act together in an assault, evidence supports the occurrence, and discrepancies are minor, common intention and joint offending are established.

issues.legal_issue: A person convicted of a minor offence arising from an old, isolated dispute may be released on probation where the circumstances make imprisonment inappropriate.
material_facts: The convictions arose from a dispute between neighbours over cleaning a drain and an incident that occurred in a fit of anger.
The incident was more than ten years old when the Supreme Court considered the request for probation.
The parties were educated and distantly related, and the Court considered imprisonment inappropriate in the circumstances.
The accused sought the benefit of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.
issues.conclusion: The convictions and sentences were maintained, but the accused were released on probation on executing bonds for good behaviour.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, and considered the age and circumstances of the incident, the trivial nature of the dispute, the parties’ background and relationship, and whether imprisonment was necessary.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_under_review and minor_offence_arose_from_trivial_dispute and incident_is_old and circumstances_make_imprisonment_inappropriate and probation_requested

predicates.criminal_conviction_under_review: A court is considering the disposition of a person who has been convicted in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.minor_offence_arose_from_trivial_dispute: The offence arose from a relatively minor dispute between the people involved.
predicates.incident_is_old: A substantial period has passed since the incident.
predicates.circumstances_make_imprisonment_inapprop: The circumstances of the incident and the people involved make imprisonment unnecessary or inappropriate.
predicates.probation_requested: The convicted person asks to be dealt with on probation.

issues.definition: When a conviction under review arose from a minor offence and trivial dispute, the incident is old, imprisonment is inappropriate in the circumstances, and probation is requested, the convicted person is released on probation.
